speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome).

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle then knee), urethritis (pain with urination), and the patient's recent sexual history with inconsistent condom use is highly suggestive of reactive arthritis, which typically follows a genitourinary or gastrointestinal infection. The family history of rheumatoid arthritis is a distractor, as RA is usually polyarticular and symmetric. I would like to see the results of a Urinalysis and a Swab for Gonorrhea/Chlamydia to confirm the infectious trigger. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine_Nucleic_Acid_Amplification_Test
